'''Amalia Patanè''' is a professor of physics at the [[University of Nottingham]] (since 2011) and the UK Director of the [[European Magnetic Field Laboratory]] partnership (since 2015).<ref name="nottingham.ac.uk">{{Cite web |title=Professor Amalia Patanè becomes the UK Director of the European Magnetic Field Laboratory (EMFL) partnership - The University of Nottingham |url=https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/physics/news/professor-amalia-patan%C3%A8-becomes-the-uk-director-of-the-european-magnetic-field-laboratory-emfl-partnership.aspx |access-date=2023-05-24 |website=www.nottingham.ac.uk}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Patanè was born in [[Nettuno]], [[Italy]], where she grew up studying [[physics]] and [[piano]],<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Patanè |first1=Amalia |last2=Fromhold |first2=Mark |date=2006-12-15 |title=Novel regimes of electron dynamics in superlattices |url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsta.2006.1886 |journal=Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences |language=en |volume=364 |issue=1849 |pages=3477–3492 |doi=10.1098/rsta.2006.1886 |pmid=17090471 |bibcode=2006RSPTA.364.3477P |s2cid=23611369 |issn=1364-503X|url-access=subscription }}</ref> first becoming interested in science during high school.<ref name=":0" /> She was an undergraduate Physics student and doctoral researcher at the [[Sapienza University of Rome]]. During her doctorate, she investigated quantum phenomena in [[nanomaterials]].

== Research and career ==
After completing her PhD in 1998 at the [[Sapienza University of Rome]], she went on to complete the United Kingdom's [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]] (EPSRC) Advanced Research Fellowship (2004–09) and Leverhulme Trust Fellowship (2017–19), as well as the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] fellowship (2018–19). Since then, she has focused her research on quantum systems. Her quantum transport studies of nanomaterials at high magnetic fields have been used to probe [[charge carriers]] in quantum confined structures. She also developed magneto-tunnelling [[spectroscopy]] techniques,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Vdovin |first1=E. E. |last2=Levin |first2=A. |last3=Patanè |first3=A. |last4=Eaves |first4=L. |last5=Main |first5=P. C. |last6=Khanin |first6=Yu. N. |last7=Dubrovskii |first7=Yu. V. |last8=Henini |first8=M. |last9=Hill |first9=G. |date=2000-10-06 |title=Imaging the Electron Wave Function in Self-Assembled Quantum Dots |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.290.5489.122 |journal=Science |language=en |volume=290 |issue=5489 |pages=122–124 |doi=10.1126/science.290.5489.122 |pmid=11021794 |bibcode=2000Sci...290..122V |issn=0036-8075|url-access=subscription }}</ref> contributing to the understanding of the collective behaviour of [[Electron|electrons]] which underpin charge ordering, [[quantum chaos]], and [[superconductivity]]. 

Patanè researched magnetic fields at [[Nottingham]] and at the [[European Magnetic Field Laboratory]] (EMFL),<ref name="nottingham.ac.uk"/> as well as leading research on [[Two-dimensional semiconductor|2D semiconductors]]. She initiated and led an EPSRC proposal for the development of EPI2SEM, a UK facility for the growth and in-situ analysis of 2D semiconductors. EPI2SEM combines the [[Epitaxy|epitaxial growth]] of [[2d semiconductors|2D semiconductors]] with in-situ chemical analysis and imaging/[[spectroscopy]] of the grown materials by [[scanning probe microscopy]] and [[electron spectroscopy]] for chemical analysis.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Grant awards |url=https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/research/beacons-of-excellence/propulsion-futures/grant-awards/ |access-date=2023-05-24 |website=www.nottingham.ac.uk}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=News - Scienta Omicron |url=https://scientaomicron.com/en/news/news/University%20of%20Nottingham%20New%20MIP%20for%20Epitaxial%20Growth%20and%20In-situ%20Analysis%20of%202D%20Semiconductors/9313?page=4 |access-date=2023-05-24 |website=scientaomicron.com}}</ref>

Patanè is currently working with a team of UK scientists at [[Queen Mary University of London]], the University of Nottingham, and the [[University of Glasgow]] on semiconductors intended to reduce electricity consumption in AI data centers and high-performance computing. The “Enabling Net Zero and the AI Revolution with Ultra-Low Energy 2D Materials and Devices (NEED2D)” EPSRC programme will involve several research institutions and manufacturers to develop new semiconductors and prototype [[Low-power electronics|low-energy electronic]] devices.<ref>{{Cite web |title=News - UK scientists to tackle AI’s surging energy costs with atom-thin semiconductors - University of Nottingham |url=https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/news/uk-scientists-to-tackle-ais-surging-energy-costs-with-atom-thin-semiconductors |access-date=2026-05-30 |website=www.nottingham.ac.uk}}</ref>  

Patanè has worked with EU Graphene Flagship, RS International projects, and training networks (e.g. Initial Training Networks funded by the EU Horizon 2020 [[Marie Curie|Marie Skłodowska-Curie]] Actions and Centres for Doctoral Training). She is a member of national and international committees, including the Commission 8 (C8: Semiconductors) of the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]] (IUPAP) as a member (2015–18) and Vice Chair (2018–21). As a member of the EMFL Council and UK Director of the EMFL, she contributes to the development of high magnetic fields and access to them for the research community.{{fact|date=May 2026}}<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 June 2026 |title=Amalia Patane |url=https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/physics/people/amalia.patane |url-status=live |access-date=3 June 2026 |website=University of Nottingham}}</ref>

== Awards and Honours ==
* 2004 EPSRC Advanced Research Fellowship
* 2007 Institute of Physics Boys medal and prize<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/bronze-early-career-medals/henry-moseley-medal-and-prize-recipients#gref|title=Henry Moseley Medal and Prize recipients &#124; Institute of Physics}}</ref>
* 2015 Council Member of the European Magnetic Field Laboratory (EMFL)
* 2015 UK Director of the EMFL Partnership
* 2017 Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowship<ref>{{Cite web |title=Research Fellowships 2017 {{!}} The Leverhulme Trust |url=https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/research-fellowships-2017 |access-date=2023-05-24 |website=www.leverhulme.ac.uk}}</ref>
* 2018 President's International Fellowship Award<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 2023|title=Professor Amalia Patanè |url=https://www.royce.ac.uk/about-royce/people/professor-amalia-patane/ |access-date=2023-05-24 |website=Henry Royce Institute |language=en}}</ref>
* 2018 Vice Chair of Commission 8 (C8: Semiconductors), International Union of Pure and Applied Physics (IUPAP)
* 2019 Honorary Professorship at the Institute of Semiconductors, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing
